issues.title: Logic inversion in hasPendingInviteByUserId method
issues.description: The hasPendingInviteByUserId method checks for accepted:true memberships instead of accepted:false (pending invites). This inverts the method's logic - it will return true when users have accepted team memberships rather than pending invites. This breaks the onboarding flow for users with team invites, causing users with accepted memberships to be redirected to personal onboarding instead of users with pending invites. The method name and its intended purpose clearly indicate it should check for pending (non-accepted) invites.

issues.title: Incorrect conditional operator in onboarding redirect logic
issues.description: The conditional logic for redirecting users with pending invites uses OR (||) instead of AND (&&). This means users will be redirected to '/onboarding/personal/settings' if they have a pending invite OR if onboarding-v3 is enabled, rather than requiring both conditions. This breaks the normal onboarding flow - any user with onboarding-v3 enabled will be incorrectly redirected to personal settings regardless of whether they have pending invites. The intended behavior was to only redirect users who have both onboarding-v3 enabled AND a pending invite.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #26829 - fix: add server-side redirect for users with pending invites on onboarding page

structured_output.summary:
The PR tries to stop users who signed up through a team invite from landing on the plan-selection page at /onboarding/getting-started. It adds a server-side redirect in that page, moves the pending-invite lookup into a new static MembershipRepository.hasPendingInviteByUserId, and switches checkOnboardingRedirect in onboardingUtils.ts from a direct prisma query to that repository method. It also adds integration tests for the new method.

The core logic is wrong. The new method filters on `accepted: true` even though its name, the PR description, and the replaced code all mean pending invites (`accepted: false`). Because the same helper feeds both the new page redirect and checkOnboardingRedirect, any user with an accepted team membership is now sent to personal onboarding, and the onboardingUtils.ts change turns `&&` into `||`, so every user is sent there whenever onboarding-v3 is enabled, with or without an invite. The integration tests would fail against this implementation, and one of them has a conditional assertion that can pass for the wrong reason. The PR also mixes in unrelated formatting churn. I would not merge this as written.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The new helper's `accepted: true` filter inverts the intended pending-invite check. That breaks the new page redirect for accepted members and, through checkOnboardingRedirect, changes routing for users who have no invite at all. The `&&` to `||` change in onboardingUtils.ts is a second, independent regression that routes every onboarding-v3 user past plan selection. The integration tests contradict the implementation, so the PR's claim of test coverage does not hold.

architecture.overview:
Users who finish signup reach the web app's onboarding routes, which are server components. The shared helper checkOnboardingRedirect in packages/features/auth/lib/onboardingUtils.ts decides which onboarding path a user should see, and it is called from apps/web/app/page.tsx and the event-types page. Before this PR, that helper used a direct prisma.membership.findFirst with accepted: false to detect pending invites, and it only routed to personal onboarding when onboarding-v3 was also enabled. Membership queries are meant to live in MembershipRepository, which is why the PR moves the lookup there.

The PR adds a second caller: the server page /onboarding/getting-started now checks for a pending invite before rendering OnboardingView, and redirects to /onboarding/personal/settings if one exists. Both callers depend on the same new static method, MembershipRepository.hasPendingInviteByUserId. That method is where the defect sits: it filters on accepted: true, so it answers 'does this user have any accepted membership' rather than 'does this user have a pending invite'.
steps: Entry point: a signed-up user lands on an onboarding route. apps/web/app/page.tsx and the event-types page call checkOnboardingRedirect, and the getting-started page calls the repository directly.

checkOnboardingRedirect (onboardingUtils.ts) loads the user, applies the completedOnboarding/org/date gate, checks email verification, and then asks MembershipRepository.hasPendingInviteByUserId whether the user has an invite. The PR changes the branch condition from && to ||.

The new static MembershipRepository.hasPendingInviteByUserId runs a findFirst on membership with accepted: true (line 588). This is the inverted filter; it should be accepted: false to match the old query and the PR's intent.
The getting-started server page (page.tsx) calls the same helper and redirects to /onboarding/personal/settings when it returns true, so it would redirect accepted members, not only invitees.

Tests: MembershipRepository.integration-test.ts asserts pending-only returns true and accepted-only returns false. Against the current implementation those two assertions fail, and the mixed-membership test's expectation is conditional on whether a second team exists.

findings.title: Pending-invite check filters on accepted: true, inverting the intended behavior
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/membership/repositories/MembershipRepository.ts`, the static method `hasPendingInviteByUserId` (around lines 584-595) filters the membership query with `accepted: true`. It should check for pending invites, so change that filter to `accepted: false`, matching the query it replaces in `packages/features/auth/lib/onboardingUtils.ts`. Keep the rest of the method as is. Then rerun the integration tests in `MembershipRepository.integration-test.ts`, which assert that pending-only returns true and accepted-only returns false.

findings.title: Branch condition changed from && to || in checkOnboardingRedirect
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/auth/lib/onboardingUtils.ts`, `checkOnboardingRedirect` (around lines 67-73) now returns `/onboarding/personal/settings` when `hasPendingInvite || onboardingV3Enabled`. The original logic returned that path only when the user has a pending invite AND onboarding-v3 is enabled. Restore the `&&` condition so users without an invite still get the plan-selection route. If a broader routing change is actually intended, document it in the PR description and add tests for users with no invite.

findings.title: Integration tests would fail against the implementation, and one assertion is conditional
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/membership/repositories/MembershipRepository.integration-test.ts`, the test 'should return true when user has both accepted and pending invites' (around lines 119-162) only creates the pending membership if a second team exists (`if (team2)`), and then asserts `expect(result).toBe(team2 ? true : false)`. Create a second team deterministically (as `beforeAll` already does for `testTeamId`), always create the pending membership, and assert `toBe(true)` unconditionally. Also fix the assertions that will fail once the repository filter is corrected.

findings.title: Static method uses the global prisma instead of the injected client
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/membership/repositories/MembershipRepository.ts`, `hasPendingInviteByUserId` (around lines 584-595) is `static` and queries the module-level `prisma`. The class injects a `prismaClient` through its constructor (line 94), and the other query methods use `this.prismaClient`. Make the method an instance method that uses `this.prismaClient`, then update callers in `onboardingUtils.ts` and `getting-started/page.tsx` to construct `new MembershipRepository()` (or reuse an existing instance), following the `new UserRepository(prisma)` pattern used in `onboardingUtils.ts`.

findings.title: Page comment says pending invites, but the query looks for accepted memberships
findings.body:
The comment above the new redirect says it handles users with pending team invites. The helper it calls matches accepted memberships (see the critical finding above), so the comment describes intent rather than the code. Once the filter is fixed the comment will be accurate, but right now a reviewer reading the page would trust the wrong behavior.

::diff{file="apps/web/app/(use-page-wrapper)/onboarding/getting-started/page.tsx" lines="28-33"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `apps/web/app/(use-page-wrapper)/onboarding/getting-started/page.tsx`, the comment above the `hasPendingInviteByUserId` call (lines 28-29) says the redirect handles users with pending team invites. Once the repository method is fixed to check `accepted: false`, the comment will be accurate. Verify that after the fix, and reword the comment if the redirect's scope differs from what it says (for example, if it should also check that the user has not completed onboarding).

findings.title: Integration tests leak users and mutate shared team data on failure
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/membership/repositories/MembershipRepository.integration-test.ts`, each `it` block creates a user and deletes it at the end of the test body (for example, lines 50-75). A failed assertion skips the delete and leaves the user and memberships behind. Track created user IDs in an array like `createdMembershipIds` and delete them in `afterEach`, so cleanup runs even when an assertion throws. Keep the existing `clearTestMemberships` pattern.

findings.title: Unrelated formatting churn mixed into the functional change
findings.body:
Several edits in this PR have nothing to do with the fix, which makes the diff harder to review:
- The page file changes the double-quoted `""` to single-quoted `''` on the `userEmail` line, which the rest of the file does not do.
- The import blocks in the page and in `MembershipRepository.ts` are reordered, and `prisma` is moved in the `@calcom/prisma` import list.
- `checkIfFeatureIsEnabledGlobally` and `hasAcceptedMembershipByEmail` are reformatted without any behavioral change.

These should be dropped or split into a separate formatting commit.

::diff{file="apps/web/app/(use-page-wrapper)/onboarding/getting-started/page.tsx" lines="35-35"}
findings.fixPrompt: Remove the unrelated formatting changes from this PR. In `apps/web/app/(use-page-wrapper)/onboarding/getting-started/page.tsx`, restore the double-quoted `""` on the `userEmail` line (line 35) and the original import ordering. In `packages/features/membership/repositories/MembershipRepository.ts`, restore the original import ordering and the original multi-line signature of `hasAcceptedMembershipByEmail`. In `packages/features/auth/lib/onboardingUtils.ts`, restore the original formatting of the `checkIfFeatureIsEnabledGlobally` call. Keep only the functional changes.

findings.title: Server-side redirect for invited users added before the plan-selection page renders
findings.body:
Putting the check in the server component means invited users are redirected before the client renders the plan-selection UI. That is the right place to prevent the payment prompt from flashing, and it removes the need for the previous client-side redirect. The idea is correct; the problem is only the filter (see the critical finding).

findings.title: Membership query moved into MembershipRepository, as the codebase intends
findings.body: Moving the pending-invite lookup out of `onboardingUtils.ts` and into `MembershipRepository` follows the project's rule that Prisma calls belong in repositories. It also gives the lookup a single definition that both the page and the shared helper can reuse. The method name and its boolean return type are clear about what the caller gets. Once the filter is fixed, this is a good structural change.
